name: CrewAI, AutoGen and Microsoft Agent Framework
question: When do I want a team of role-based agents?
summary: CrewAI defines agents by role, goal and backstory, assigns them tasks and runs them as a crew, sequentially or under a manager agent, with Flows for event-driven control. AutoGen pioneered conversational multi-agent systems; Microsoft moved it to maintenance in October 2025, and its successor, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (April 2026), merges AutoGen and Semantic Kernel for .NET and Python. AG2 continues AutoGen as a community project. Teams of agents fit genuinely parallel, separable work, and cost several times the tokens (Panel 10).
useCases: Research and content pipelines with separable roles
steps: Check that the work really splits into roles (Panel 10)
Define agents and tasks with expected outputs
Start sequential; add a manager only if needed
Measure tokens and consistency against one agent
pitfalls: Role-play prompts instead of clear tasks
remember: Teams only for work that truly divides; mind the token bill.
caption: Microsoft Agent Framework for .NET; CrewAI for Python.

practice.scenario: A fictional equity-research desk split a sector report into roles: a data analyst pulling results, an investigator reading filings, and a writer. CrewAI ran them as a crew, which worked because the parts were genuinely separable. For its UPI support agent the same team measured a two-agent crew against one agent: the crew used 3.6 times the tokens for no gain in accuracy, so support stayed a single agent.

industries.use: Separable analyst, investigator and writer roles

practice.analogy: A film crew: worth it when there really are separate jobs for a camera operator, a sound engineer and an editor, and expensive overhead for a short phone video.

library.name: CrewAI
library.what: Role-based agents, tasks, crews and flows in Python; Microsoft Agent Framework is the .NET and Azure-native alternative.

practice.note: Here the dispute itself is raised by a person after review. For new .NET or Azure work use Microsoft Agent Framework; AutoGen is in maintenance mode.

samples.code:
from crewai import Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool

@tool("Get transaction")
def get_transaction(utr: str) -> str:
    """Look up a UPI transaction by its 12-digit UTR."""
    return str(bank.transactions.get(utr))

investigator = Agent(
    role="Payments investigator",
    goal="Find out what happened to the customer's UPI debit",
    backstory="You check transaction records and never guess.",
    tools=[get_transaction], llm="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5")

writer = Agent(
    role="Support writer",
    goal="Explain the outcome clearly and say what happens next",
    backstory="You write short, plain replies for customers.",
    llm="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5")

investigate = Task(description="Investigate UTR {utr}. Customer says: {question}",
                   expected_output="Status of the payment, with evidence", agent=investigator)
reply = Task(description="Write the reply. If a dispute is needed, say it is sent for approval.",
             expected_output="A reply of at most four sentences", agent=writer,
             human_input=True)                                 # a person reviews

crew = Crew(agents=[investigator, writer], tasks=[investigate, reply],
            process=Process.sequential)
result = crew.kickoff(inputs={"utr": "412345678901", "question": QUESTION})

numericDrill.question: A single agent handles a support case with about 10,000 tokens. A two-agent crew uses 4 exchanges of about 9,000 tokens each. How many times the tokens does the crew use?
numericDrill.answer: 4 × 9,000 = 36,000 tokens against 10,000: 3.6 times. If accuracy does not improve, the crew is pure overhead. Multi-agent designs pay off only when work is genuinely separable or parallel (Panel 10).

interview.question: What happened to AutoGen?
interview.answer: Microsoft moved AutoGen to maintenance mode in October 2025, with only critical fixes. Its successor, Microsoft Agent Framework, reached 1.0 in April 2026 and merges AutoGen’s agent abstractions with Semantic Kernel’s enterprise features for .NET and Python. AG2 continues AutoGen as a community project. New work should not start on AutoGen.

interview.question: When would you pick CrewAI?
interview.answer: When the work divides naturally into roles with clear hand-offs, such as research, analysis and writing, and you want a quick, readable way to express that in Python. Use Flows for state and control around crews, start with a sequential process, and compare cost and consistency against a single agent.
